project: BTRC P0 — Characterize Runtime Opening and Record Ownership
description: Implement BTRC packet P0 by publishing a complete ownership matrix for the 44 runtime-opening behavioral dependencies, deferred factories, external effects, and late binders, and by adding deterministic characterization of current Factory Event order and terminal results across every required runtime-opening mode without changing production behavior.

context.customerAsk: Inventory and classify the current runtime-opening dependencies, deferred factories, external-effect fields, and late binders; publish the ownership matrix under docs/internal/packaged-service-structure/ as work proceeds for the parallel P1 lane; and characterize current event order and terminal results for successful and failed batch, hosted/service, replay, one-shot, ACP target, direct JavaScript, and standalone runs, including cancellation and partial failure. Make no production behavior changes.
context.problem: Factory Session opening currently performs a secondary construction pass around 44 grouped behavioral dependencies plus external-effect bags, deferred service factories, and late binding. Ownership and cleanup destinations are unclear, and current event ordering, terminal results, isolation, and failure behavior are not consistently frozen across all entry modes, creating migration risk for parallel composition packets.
context.solution: Publish a living, reconciled ownership matrix that gives every in-scope item exactly one classification and target owner or deletion, then add focused deterministic behavior tests with literal canonical Factory Event sequences and complete terminal outcomes for success and failure in each required mode. Use existing owner and root.BuildProcess/Process.Execute boundaries with injected edge fakes, preserve current production code and contracts, and keep the matrix available to P1 while both lanes proceed in parallel.

acceptanceCriteria: The published ownership matrix enumerates all 44 grouped runtime-opening behavioral dependencies, all deferred factories, every ExternalEffects field, and every late binder, and assigns each row exactly one classification and one target owner or explicit deletion.

Representative successful and failed batch, hosted/service, replay, one-shot invocation, ACP target, direct JavaScript, and standalone fixture scenarios assert literal canonical Factory Event order and complete terminal results or typed failures.
Characterization proves current concurrent-session isolation, cancellation, partial-opening failure, cleanup observation, and prevention of duplicate terminal publication.
Production behavior, public contracts, generated API artifacts, event emission, and runtime composition remain unchanged, with no broad unrelated cleanup or meta-test enforcement added.
Behavioral evidence uses deterministic owner/process boundaries and injected edge fakes rather than live services, source/topology inventories, sleeps, or self-derived expected traces.
Typecheck and focused tests pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file churn are reconciled against current main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Publish the complete ownership matrix
userStories.description: As a maintainer working in a parallel composition lane, I want one authoritative map of every runtime-opening input and binding so that I can move each behavior to the correct owner without inventing another construction path.
acceptanceCriteria: A matrix under docs/internal/packaged-service-structure/ lists all 44 grouped dependency fields, all deferred factory roles, all invocation-local external-effect fields, and all current late attachment, completion, and binding operations.

Each row records a stable item name, current role, exactly one classification (build-time dependency, operation value, private owner state, or delete), exactly one target owner or explicit deletion, lifecycle/cleanup responsibility where applicable, and the downstream retirement packet.
Documented totals and source-to-row reconciliation make omissions and duplicate rows reviewer-visible without adding a production or test-time filesystem inventory checker.
The matrix is published before all characterization is complete and remains reconciled with authoritative current main for P1 and other parallel consumers.
No destination introduces a generic factory, locator, callback injector, compatibility graph, service-valued operation bag, or exposed private owner state.
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Published docs/internal/packaged-service-structure/runtime-opening-ownership-matrix.md. It reconciles all 44 grouped dependency fields, 15 ExternalEffects fields, 38 deferred construction/callback roles, and 13 late completion/attachment/binding operations with one classification, one target owner or deletion, lifecycle/cleanup responsibility, retirement packet, and reviewer-visible source totals. No production or inventory-checker code changed.

userStories.title: Characterize batch execution outcomes
userStories.description: As a maintainer replacing runtime opening, I want the existing batch success and failure traces frozen so that later composition changes preserve the ordering and aggregate terminal result customers observe.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic representative multi-work batch records the exact canonical Factory Event type order from acceptance through dispatch and terminal session publication, including child-work and session terminal ordering.
The successful batch asserts the complete terminal status/result projection, work counts, and stable correlation/session identities currently returned.
A failed or partially failed batch asserts exact event order, per-work terminal outcomes, aggregate terminal status/result, and typed failure classification without stranded non-terminal work.
The scenarios use root.BuildProcess and Process.Execute with deterministic edge replacements and no live provider, network, or timeout-padded synchronization.
Focused batch characterization tests pass

Tests pass
userStories.notes: Added tests/functional/factory_runtime/root_composition/batch_characterization_test.go. Root-built Process.Execute runs a two-work parent/child batch through a capacity-one resource fixture and an injected provider edge; tests assert the literal 20-event success/partial-failure order, request/relation and work counts, stable ~default session and dispatch-to-Worker-Session identities, terminal per-work states, typed permanent_bad_request classification, no stranded work, and the current SUCCEEDED/FINAL aggregate session projection. Repeated focused runs pass without sleeps, network, or live providers.

userStories.notes: Added pkg/services/recordings/internal/replay/btrc_p0_characterization_test.go against the checked-in inference-events.replay.json fixture. The tests assert the literal seven-event RUN_REQUEST → WORK_REQUEST → DISPATCH_REQUEST → INFERENCE_REQUEST → INFERENCE_RESPONSE → DISPATCH_RESPONSE → RUN_RESPONSE order, IDs, sequences 0..6, ticks, reconstructed submission/dispatch/provider output, delivery tick, and ACCEPTED terminal result.
